When a post in a group you watch looks like an event, it shows up here.
EventBorg can notice when Instagram or Facebook notifies you that a local venue or a profile you watch posted a new story, or that a group you watch has a new post, and tell you it might be an event.

Only notifications from the Instagram and Facebook apps. Their title and text are checked on your phone, in memory, against your watch list and the listed venues. Notifications from every other app are ignored right away.
It never stores or sends the content of a notification, and it never downloads, reads or analyses stories. Profiles and groups you watch stay on this phone.

When a post in a group you watch looks like an event (a date, a time, a price, words like concert or tickets), its text and picture are kept on this phone for 7 days. They are sent to EventBorg only if you tap \"Add as event\".
With \"Hide original notification\" on, EventBorg removes Instagram\'s or Facebook\'s notification when its own alert replaces it, and hides posts from watched groups that don\'t look like events.
Optional, off by default: \"Share story alerts from local venues\" sends only which listed venue posted a story and when, so other users get the alert too.
EventBorg works fine without this. You can turn it off any time here or in Android\'s notification access settings.
Now turn on EventBorg in the list Android shows you, then come back.
Does Android say \"Restricted setting\"? That happens for apps installed outside the Play Store. Open App info, tap ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again.

Make Instagram\'s story notifications silent, so only EventBorg\'s alert makes a sound: Instagram\'s notification settings → Stories → Silent. Don\'t switch them off: blocked notifications never reach EventBorg.
For each profile you watch, open it in Instagram, tap the bell and turn on Story notifications. A ✓ appears on the Watching tab once the first one arrives.
For each group you watch, open it in Facebook → ⋯ → Notifications → All posts.
Tip: use a separate Instagram/Facebook account just for EventBorg follows, so your own feed stays as it is.
EventBorg stops reading notifications at once. You can also remove its access in Android settings.
